blocks.heading: Pocketing Cloth Built to Outlast the Garment Around It
blocks.intro: A tightly woven fabric for trouser, jacket and jean pockets — engineered to survive more wash and wear cycles than the outer fabric it sits behind, since a torn pocket is one of the most common garment failure points.

blocks.imageAlt: Tightly woven pocketing cloth rolls used for trouser and jacket pockets
blocks.heading: A Pocket That Fails Before the Garment Does Is a Returned Garment
blocks.html:
Pocketing cloth doesn't get noticed when it works — it only gets noticed when it splits at the corner, frays at the seam or lets a coin pocket sag after a few washes. Because pockets take constant hand contact, friction from wallets and keys, and the same wash cycles as the rest of the garment, the fabric behind them has to outlast the shell fabric it's stitched into, not just match it.

We manufacture pocketing cloth as a tightly woven, stable-construction fabric in cotton, poly-cotton and polyester options, supplied in standard rolls or custom widths to match your cutting layout. It's built for one job: hold its shape and its seams through the full working life of the garment.
checklist: Tight, stable weave resistant to tearing and seam-slip
Smooth hand-feel suited to constant hand and pocket contact
Consistent width and weight across every production batch

blocks.heading: Pocketing Cloth FAQs
blocks.intro: Have a question specific to your order? Send it to us directly and we'll respond within one business day.

items.a: Shrinkage treatment depends on the composition and the finish you order. Tell us the garment type and wash conditions your pocket needs to survive, and we'll confirm the right fabric option for that requirement.

items.q: Can you match a specific pocket fabric colour?
items.a: We supply pocketing in white, natural and dyed options depending on order quantity and availability. Share a swatch or shade reference and we'll confirm whether we can match it for your run.

items.q: What composition do you recommend for jeans vs. formal trousers?
items.a: Denim pockets generally benefit from our polyester or heavy-duty grade for added abrasion resistance, while formal trousers are often paired with cotton or poly-cotton pocketing for a softer hand-feel. We're happy to advise once we know your garment specification.

items.q: What is the minimum order quantity?
items.a: Minimum quantities vary by composition, colour and roll width. Share your requirement through our contact form and we'll confirm feasible order sizes and lead time for your specific fabric.
